title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page sits in the 1983-84 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' notes. It follows a page on anabelian conjectures for singular and stable curves and on 'anabelian compactifications' modelled on Deligne-Mumford, and precedes a page computing the profinite T^+_{0,4}, Pi_{0,3}, S_3, PSL(2,Z) and so on. The page is a programme: find generators and relations for the Teichmüller groupoids and groups. 'Teichmüller group' T_{g,nu} means the mapping class group of a genus g surface with nu punctures, or the orbifold fundamental group of M_{g,nu}. 'Special and ordinary' variants and 'toric extensions' are meant; the toric extensions are the central Z^nu extensions obtained by replacing punctures with boundary circles or tangent vectors, i.e. the !-decorated groups T^{+!}. Grothendieck expects three complementary types of presentation, each with an arithmetic meaning.

(a) Pants or 'triads' presentation. Base points are taken at the 'most critical' points at infinity of the modular stacks M_{g,nu}. These are the 0-dimensional strata of the Deligne-Mumford boundary, i.e. maximally degenerate stable curves, i.e. pants decompositions, with tangential base points there. Judging by T^{+!}_{0,4}, this is best suited to the boundary-twist (toric) versions T^{+!}_{g,nu}, or T^+_{g,I}.

(b) 'Lego box' presentation. One uses a complete (or reduced) set of basic pieces: low-dimensional modular stacks such as M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}. The generators are the automorphism groups of these pieces, i.e. finite stabilisers and orbifold points. The relations come from specific 'chains of deformations' joining pieces. Two examples are given.
- T^+_{0,4}.
- T^+_{1,1} = SL(2,Z) = <rho, sigma | rho^3 = sigma^2, rho^6 = 1>. This is the amalgam Z/6 *_{Z/2} Z/4, where rho and sigma generate the stabilisers of the elliptic curves with j = 0 and j = 1728, and rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1 is the generic elliptic involution.

(c) Presentation by involutions. These are orientation-reversing elements, lying in T^-_{g,nu}, the extended mapping class group including anticonformal maps. The typical example is the extended group T_{1,1} = GL(2,Z), viewed as an analogue of crystallographic triangle reflection groups. It is generated by three reflections r1, r2, r3 with (r1 r2)^2 = (r2 r3)^3 and (r1 r2)^4 = (r2 r3)^6 = 1. This is the presentation GL(2,Z) = D_4 *_{V_4} D_6. It is a central ±1 extension of the (2,3,infinity) reflection triangle group PGL(2,Z). The rotations r1r2 and r2r3 recover the sigma and rho of (b).

Purpose: supply the group-theoretic skeleton of the Teichmüller tower, so that the action of Gal(Qbar/Q), or of GT, can be described on generators. Each type of presentation is tied to an arithmetic structure:
- tangential base points at degenerate curves for (a);
- finite automorphism groups / CM points for (b);
- real structures / complex conjugation for (c).
errors: (c) The relations r_i^2 = 1 are left implicit ('réflexions'). The product r1 r3 has infinite order, a parabolic corresponding to the cusp, so this is a non-finite Coxeter-like amalgam rather than a finite triangle group. With r_i^2 = 1 added, the presentation is correct (GL(2,Z) = D4 *_{V4} D6).
(b) The SL(2,Z) presentation <rho, sigma | rho^3 = sigma^2, rho^6 = 1> is correct; sigma^4 = 1 is then a consequence.
The page gives no actual presentation of T^+_{0,4} or T^{+!}_{0,4}; it is only cited as an example.

ideas.what: Presentation of Teichmüller groupoids via pants decompositions, with base points at maximally degenerate stable curves ('most critical points at infinity')
ideas.modern_name: Pants-decomposition complex presentation; tangential base points at maximal degeneration; Moore-Seiberg / Hatcher-Thurston / Bakalov-Kirillov Lego-Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher-Thurston 1980; Moore-Seiberg 1989; Ihara-Nakamura (Galois action, maximal degeneration); Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps 2000; Bakalov-Kirillov 2000
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2 (Teichmüller tower, base points at infinity, pants decompositions)

ideas.what: Lego presentation: Teichmüller tower generated by automorphism groups of basic pieces (M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}) plus deformation chains, e.g. SL(2,Z) = Z/6 *_{Z/2} Z/4
ideas.modern_name: Lego-Teichmüller game; generation of the tower by modular dimension ≤1, relations from dimension ≤2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), proved by Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Bakalov-Kirillov; SL(2,Z) amalgam classical (Serre, Trees)

ideas.what: Presentations of extended Teichmüller groups T^- by orientation-reversing involutions, by analogy with reflection triangle groups; GL(2,Z) = <r1,r2,r3> with dihedral relations
ideas.modern_name: Generation of extended mapping class groups by (orientation-reversing) involutions / Coxeter-type presentations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Generation results: Stukow (extended MCG generated by 3 symmetries, ~2004), Brendle-Farb, Kassabov (involutions); GL(2,Z) amalgam classical
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions anticonformal/extended groups only briefly, if at all; unsure

ideas.what: Claim that all three presentation types carry arithmetic meaning (Galois/GT action)
ideas.modern_name: GT-action on mapping class groups; complex conjugation as an element of GT

missed.claim: A programme for presenting the extended Teichmüller tower (including anticonformal maps) by involutions with Coxeter-like relations, generalising GL(2,Z) = triangle-group extension, and giving these an arithmetic meaning (real structures, complex conjugation in Gal(Qbar/Q)). Generation by involutions is known, but a systematic 'reflection-group' presentation of the whole extended tower, compatible with Lego gluing and tied to the GT action with complex conjugation, is not standard.
missed.quote: Présentations par involutions, qui sont dans T^-_{gν}. Exemple typique T_{11} ≃ Gl(2,Z) (Analogie aux groupes cristallographiques triangulés)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could connect real moduli spaces and anticonformal symmetries (real algebraic curves, Klein surfaces) with the GT / anabelian Teichmüller tower. It would also give Coxeter-type presentations of extended mapping class groups adapted to Galois actions.

missed.claim: The three presentations are seen as complementary facets of one structure: tangential points at maximal degeneration (a), orbifold/automorphism points (b), and real/reflection structure (c). Later literature developed (a) and (b) jointly (Lego-Teichmüller) but did not systematically pair them with (c).
missed.quote: trois types de présentations, à propriétés complémentaires — mais toutes à significations arithmétiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a unified treatment of the GT action including complex conjugation and the extended (anticonformal) Teichmüller groupoid.

deep.surprise_reason: Items (a) and (b) are the Esquisse Lego-Teichmüller programme, later realised by Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps and Bakalov-Kirillov. The third type, involution/reflection presentations of the extended tower with an announced arithmetic meaning, is a less-known unpublished thread. It is only sketched via the classical GL(2,Z) example.
transcription_corrections: 'significations arithmétiques' fits the image ('signifcations arithmétiques'); keep.
'(Analogie aux groupes cristallographiques triangulés)' is probably 'triangulaires' (triangle groups).
'à l'aide des {+groupes d'+}automorphismes': the insertion 'groupes d'' is written above 'automorphismes', which is underlined.
'voir des boîtes encore plus complètes {+réduites+}': the image suggests a correction between 'plus complètes' and 'réduites'; uncertain which is retained.
'T_{g\nu}' in (c) should be read T^-_{g,ν}; 'T_{11}' is the full (extended) T_{1,1}.
